gloss: sour grapes; poor loser attitude; excuses

definitions.explanation: Making excuses or disparaging something after failing to obtain it; refusing to accept defeat gracefully.

examples.japanese: それは{負|ま}け{惜|お}しみに{聞|き}こえる。
{負|ま}け{惜|お}しみを{言|い}うな。
examples.english: Don't be a sore loser./Stop making excuses.

examples.japanese: {負|ま}け{惜|お}しみかもしれないが、あの{仕事|しごと}は{自分|じぶん}に{合|あ}わなかった。
examples.english: It might be sour grapes, but that job wasn't right for me.

examples.japanese: {負|ま}け{惜|お}しみが{強|つよ}い{人|ひと}は{嫌|きら}われやすい。
examples.english: People who are sore losers tend to be disliked.

examples.japanese: 「あの{大学|だいがく}には{最初|さいしょ}から{行|い}きたくなかった」と{言|い}うのは{負|ま}け{惜|お}しみだろう。
examples.english: Saying "I never wanted to go to that university anyway" is probably just sour grapes.

notes:
FORMS:
{負|ま}け (defeat) + {惜|お}しむ (to regret, grudge) → regretting defeat = sour grapes

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {負|ま}け{惜|お}しみを{言|い}う - to make excuses after losing
- {負|ま}け{惜|お}しみに{聞|き}こえる - to sound like sour grapes
- {負|ま}け{惜|お}しみが{強|つよ}い - to be a bad loser

USAGE:
Used when someone refuses to accept failure gracefully and instead makes excuses or criticizes what they couldn't get. Similar to the English "sour grapes" from Aesop's fable.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {強|つよ}がり - putting on a brave face (hiding vulnerability)
- {負|ま}け{惜|お}しみ - sour grapes (making excuses for failure)
